rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every pronoun/demonstrative resolves in-chunk (chunk 2 'it'→AI named same chunk; chunk 3 'it'/'the result'→agent/change named same chunk; chunk 7 'it'→'the limit' same sentence). Cross-chunk reuse is compliant reuse, not a violation: chunk 9's 'an unfamiliar codebase' verbatim-reuses the phrase chunk 3 coined six slides earlier (rule 1's explicit non-violation case), and chunk 9's 'the progression'/'the leverage model' name chunks 1 and 8 by their own section titles. Chunk 1's 'Six levels, from assistance to a system you keep improving' is a self-contained overview clause (not a referring pronoun needing an antecedent) whose two endpoints are immediately cashed out by the very next chunk header ('Assistance') and, seven chunks later, 'Improving the system' — a reader is never stranded mid-read.

No body sentence points at another file by position. The two external citations (chunk 1's Wollsén/McCrosky playbook, chunk 8's Wollsén throughput post) are both named with title + link, not located positionally. All within-file backward references (chunk 9) name their target by section title, matching the rule's own passing example shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw/caught' beat-reference construction anywhere in body (grep for you did|saw|caught|built|wrote|ran|made returned only the third-person Wollsén citation, not a student-beat reference). This is a supplementary reading with no session-beat callbacks to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File contains no guess/predict-then-reveal instruction (grep for guess|predict returned no body hits). Nothing for this rule to check.

Every chunk carries a self-sufficient claim, including the short closer (chunk 9's two sentences state the Part1/Part2 identity outright). No chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Each level header (Assistance, Interactive work, Delegating bounded outcomes, Directing parallel sessions, Encoding checked loops, Improving the system) is a literally true summary of its chunk's content, as are 'Part 1: The progression', 'Part 2: The leverage model', and 'One model, not two' (which states exactly that the two parts are one model).

Checked all six sub-items per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere; no anaphora/epistrophe triples (chunk 8's four bullets each open differently, not a triplet cadence); no self-grading superlatives (grep-equivalent scan found none — the value-prop leak sub-item is clean); no number-with-retraction pattern (the 30-40/10-15 session counts and 3-4x estimate in chunk 8 are precise attributed citations from the source, not a hedged-then-retracted figure); no abstraction-noun stacks (vocabulary stays concrete: 'worktrees', 'checks', 'a diff'); no verb triplet with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo-internal vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood) anywhere in body. Terms used ('context', 'memory', 'skills', 'verification', 'worktrees', 'checks') are AE101 spine vocabulary and ordinary engineering terms for this audience, not maintainer dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunks 2-6 and 9 each carry exactly one bolded handle ('**Moves you up:**'), within the ≤1 budget. Chunk 8 carries two bolded handles ('**Reach**', '**Calibration**') on a consolidation slide defining the model's two named axes — the rule's own exception ('a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law') covers exactly this shape. No whole-sentence bolding anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `grep -n "supplementary" site/layouts/slides.js`, which shows the deck builder has first-class handling for supplementary pages (id prefix 'supplementary-', kind code 'S...'), unlike the 2026-07-09 incident where prework/supplementary/reference sections were dropped. This file's section is not phase-less prose stranded outside the deck model.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/agentic-engineering-progression.md` → output 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' 'Part 1'/'Part 2' are consecutive content labels for the file's two sections, not hand-numbered slide positions, and no in-file 'Phase K'/'Step K' references exist to go stale.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/agentic-engineering-progression.md` → output 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Exit 0. No 'below/above/further down/top of this' pointers in body (grep confirms).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File contains only two external links (both named-by-title citations to Wollsén's posts), no in-page fragment links to check against the anchor-index mechanism this rule documents. Rule 13 is explicitly a review surface, never a gate, and there is nothing here to review.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/agentic-engineering-progression.md` → output 'files: 1  slides: 9  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets  oversized: 0' and '✓ every slide is within limits'.
